jane (platform): Heads-up: tenant T-443 triggered eviction twice this morning; our soft-evict path didn't kick in like we expected. Anyone have time to triage? cc @kevin @maria
kevin (infra): On it. quick q: which path should be authoritative for eviction decisions — rate-limiter or fairness-scheduler? we currently duplicate thresholds.
maria (runtime): I'd vote fairness-scheduler -> single source. rate-limiter should be admission-only: pass/fail at frontend. eviction decision requires history + anomaly features.
jane (platform): Agree. But we need deterministic behavior when services disagree. We saw a race where RL admitted burst, scheduler later evicted, causing user 503s.
sam (sre): We should prefer 'graceful ejection' instead of hard kill. degrade to best-effort: reduce concurrency, apply per-tenant tail-latency cap, then evict.
kevin (infra): Tradeoff: graceful path increases shared latency under heavy abuse. If we don't evict fast, SLOs for other tenants blow up.
maria (runtime): Proposal: two-phase decision. short-window anomaly detector in rate-limiter raises an 'abuse-alert' event. scheduler runs policy that either 'throttle', 'deprioritize', or 'evict' based on aggregated score.
jane (platform): Score composition idea: 40% request-rate spike, 30% cost-per-token anomaly, 20% KV-cache-skip-rate, 10% auth-failure ratio. Thoughts?
eve (security): Need to add 'rule-evidence' so we can audit why we evicted. Include rule id + window + metric snapshot.
kevin (infra): Config sketch:
```
eviction_policy:
  window_sec: 60
  spike_threshold: 5.0
  scoring_weights: [0.4,0.3,0.2,0.1]
  soft_actions: [throttle, deprioritize]
  hard_action: evict
  audit: true
```
ops-bot: ratebot: T-443: 6.1x spike in 60s, cache_skip 0.52, cost_per_token +210% — recommended action: deprioritize -> 10% capacity
sam (sre): Let's not auto-evict in prod without manual review; canary to 1% auto-eject for low-impact tenants.
maria (runtime): Implementation note: make 'eviction' an output event with deterministic id so we can rollback by issuing 'reinstate <id>'. Avoid implicit state in multiple services.
jane (platform): Action items: kevin to prototype event schema, maria to add scoring library, sam to craft canary runbook, eve to write audit format. I'll open RFC follow-up.
kevin (infra): I'll add an initial PR for schema today. ping me if you want in design review.
jane (platform): :thumbsup:
